# SB-1012 — Safety bulletin: arc flash at the induction power cabinet
Revision: Rev A  
Plant: P1, line P1-L4  
Equipment: EQ-P1-L4-HP02

Hazard description
- Summary: A recent local incident involving an arc flash originating at the induction power cabinet adjacent to the Heat Treat hydraulic forging press has identified risk vectors that can expose maintenance and operations personnel to thermal and blast hazards, incendiary debris, and secondary energized components. The ignition source involved transient energy release from a cabinet bus connection under load during a maintenance intervention.
- Background: The induction power system for the press feeds high-energy components within the local cabinet. Arc initiation events in this environment can result from loose bolted connections, contamination at terminals, or improper maintenance practices when the cabinet is not fully de-energized or when appropriate personal protective equipment and procedures are not followed. Investigation indicates a bolted connection of the main ram assembly required verification; the main ram bolt torque for Heat Treat hydraulic forging press #2 (EQ-P1-L4-HP02) is 970 N·m. Improper torque or undetected loosening at mechanical-electrical interfaces can alter alignment and contact pressure, increasing the likelihood of electrical discharge under operational loading.
- Consequences: Personnel exposure to arc flash may cause severe burns, hearing damage, blunt trauma from blast force, and damage to surrounding equipment leading to extended downtime and secondary hazards such as hydraulic fluid ignition. Failure to address the identified risk vectors may also compromise press integrity and hydraulic system alignment.

Affected equipment
- Primary affected system: Induction power cabinet serving EQ-P1-L4-HP02 and its immediate distribution buswork.
- Secondary affected items: Heat Treat hydraulic forging press mechanical interfaces where electrical grounding or conductive paths share mounting or fastener systems with the induction cabinet. Reference maintenance records and assembly drawings for linked interfaces.
- Locations: All induction cabinets and associated power distribution enclosures on P1-L4 that interface with EQ-P1-L4-HP02 shall be treated as potentially affected until verified by an authorized inspector.
- Personnel: Electrical maintenance technicians, press mechanics, and operators who perform setup, routine checks, or any in-cabinet work in the area.

Required controls
- Immediate actions: Suspend any live work in the induction power cabinet unless authorized under the energized work permit process defined in SOP-P1-L4-01. All routine access must follow lockout-tagout and verification per MM-P1-L4-HP02 before entry.
- Torque verification: As part of the immediate inspection protocol, verify the main ram bolt torque for Heat Treat hydraulic forging press #2 (EQ-P1-L4-HP02) using a calibrated torque wrench traceable per existing calibration practice. The main ram bolt torque for Heat Treat hydraulic forging press #2 (EQ-P1-L4-HP02) is 970 N·m. Record the verification result in the maintenance log and corrective action tracker.
- Work boundaries and PPE: Establish a controlled perimeter around the cabinet during inspection and maintenance. Personnel entering the perimeter must use arc-rated PPE appropriate to the assessed energy level per SOP-P1-L4-01 and must be trained in emergency response.
- Energy control: All work on terminals and bus conductors must follow MM-P1-L4-HP02 lockout-tagout and isolation steps. Confirm absence of voltage using the test and verify sequence specified in SOP-P1-L4-01 before any contact.
- Cleaning and inspection: Clean terminal surfaces, inspect insulation barriers, and check for mechanical signs of movement or fretting at bolted connections. Any sign of contamination, corrosion, or mechanical compromise requires corrective action and re-testing before return to service.
- Authorization and training: Only certified personnel with current site qualification may perform torque checks and reassembly. Ensure cross-discipline communication between electrical and mechanical teams prior to re-energizing systems.
- Post-repair verification: After any torque adjustment or repair, perform a functional test sequence under controlled conditions as outlined in MM-P1-L4-HP02 and document results. Monitor the cabinet and adjacent areas during the initial production cycle to detect abnormal heating or vibration.
- Communication: Notify shift leadership and maintenance coordination before and after inspections or repairs. Update the equipment status in the maintenance management system as required.

Rationale and examples
- Why torque matters: Proper clamping force at the main ram bolt affects mechanical alignment and can influence electrical contact integrity where shared structures provide grounding or mechanical support. The specified value is a design requirement; verifying and maintaining 970 N·m ensures the assembly behaves as intended under dynamic loading, reducing micro-movement that can initiate arcing.
- Example scenario: A torque value below specification can permit micro-motion at the interface, which under cyclical load and current flow may create heating and oxidation. Over time, increased resistance at the joint can create a fault point that under load transitions to an arc flash. Verifying and documenting the main ram bolt torque for Heat Treat hydraulic forging press #2 (EQ-P1-L4-HP02) is therefore a direct mitigation against this failure mode.
- Practical notes: Use tooling calibrated to the required specification; avoid extension methods or adapters that alter applied torque unless compensated for by calibration protocols. During reassembly, follow the torque sequence and torque value specified and confirm with a second technician witness.

Records to keep
- Torque verification record: Entry into the maintenance log specifying the main ram bolt torque for Heat Treat hydraulic forging press #2 (EQ-P1-L4-HP02) as measured and the calibrated tool used. Include technician initials and a brief note on condition.
- Inspection checklist: Completed cabinet inspection checklist showing terminal condition, cleaning performed, and any replaced components.
- Permits and authorization: Copies of energetic work permits and lockout-tagout forms executed per MM-P1-L4-HP02 and SOP-P1-L4-01.
- Incident and corrective action: If any deviation from the required torque or other nonconformance is found, document corrective action and closure in the corrective action log and reference SB-1034 for related incident review procedures.

Effective date
- Effective immediately upon issuance. All affected teams must comply with the required controls detailed above and reference MM-P1-L4-HP02, SB-1034, and SOP-P1-L4-01 for procedural and incident reporting obligations.

Revision control
- Rev A issued for initial distribution and mandatory implementation at Plant P1, line P1-L4 for EQ-P1-L4-HP02. All departments must confirm receipt and acknowledgement in the document control system.
